History: Cilicia was the coastal region of southeastern Asia Minor, home of Tarsus. Men from the synagogue of the Cilicians disputed with Stephen, and Paul — a Cilician by birth — travelled through Cilicia strengthening the churches.
Culture: Greek-Roman cities; Tarsus was a noted centre of learning, and Paul calls himself a citizen of no mean city.
Religion: Pagan cults alongside a Jewish community strong enough to have its own synagogue in Jerusalem.
BibleConnection: Cilicians appear as Stephen's disputants and as Paul's home people; the letter of the Jerusalem Council was addressed to the brethren in Cilicia as well as Syria.
